answer_to_user:
I ran three separate screens — banks, utilities, and REITs — each ranked by dividend RELIABILITY (no-cut streak within the ~10-year tracked window) rather than by raw yield, so we compare on safety-adjusted income, and you can see the country spread in each.

BANKS: highest-yield reliable payers skew to China/Europe — China Merchants Bank (600036.CG) ~10.3% with a 10-yr no-cut streak and ~47% payout, Credit Agricole (ACA.PA, France) ~8.9% at ~56% payout, then US regionals at more modest yields — TFS Financial (TFSL.US) ~6.4%, Union Bankshares (UNB.US) ~6.0%, Flushing Financial (FFIC.US) ~5.7%, all 10-yr streaks. Banks generally pay ~50-70% of earnings, so payout ratios here look moderate/coverable.

UTILITIES: Italian/UK-listed names lead — A2A (0N54.LSE, Italy) ~7.6% at ~48% payout, Star Gas Partners (SGU.US) ~6.3%, Iren (0MUN.LSE) ~6.25%, Acea (0MHD.LSE) ~5.9%, Enel (ENL.XETRA, Italy) ~5.5% but payout ~1.08 (over 100% of earnings — worth watching). Utilities as a group show steady ~40-60% payouts and full 10-yr streaks — structurally the most 'boring/reliable' of the three.

REITs: highest headline yields — Community Healthcare Trust (CHCT.US) ~11.9%, Nexpoint Residential (NXRT.US) ~8.7%, Primary Health Properties (PHP.LSE, UK) ~7.6%, One Liberty (OLP.US) ~7.5%, plus Japanese REITs ~7%. BUT the payout ratios look alarming on an EPS basis (CHCT ~1.44, PHP ~1.21, OLP ~1.24, NXRT ~47) — that is NORMAL for REITs because they distribute most of their cash flow and depreciation depresses EPS; you must judge REIT safety on FFO/cash-flow coverage, not the EPS payout shown here. So you can't naively compare a REIT's 'payout ratio' to a bank's.

Bottom line on 'most reliable yield': utilities offer the cleanest reliability-per-yield (moderate payout, full streaks); banks give solid mid-single-digit yields with coverable payouts (higher in China/Europe); REITs offer the highest headline yields but require a cash-flow lens to judge safety. All reliability claims here are bounded by the ~10-year history window I can see — I can't verify longer streaks. Not investment advice.
